labellers.a: an AI labeller, independent and blind: it read only protocol.md, sheets.txt and the sheet images (no time, date or file name on a sheet, the camera's caption covered) and never saw the other labeller's file, sample.json, the frames, an earlier labels file or any extractor output
labellers.b: an AI labeller, independent and blind: it read only protocol.md, sheets.txt and the sheet images (no time, date or file name on a sheet, the camera's caption covered) and never saw the other labeller's file, sample.json, the frames, an earlier labels file or any extractor output

protocol.frames: every Rainier live capture of 19-22 Nov 2026 local time with the Sun at or above 3 deg (geometric, oculus-core, at the manifest camera): 105 frames, one sheet each, ids in a seeded shuffle (sample.json)

bands.summit: the plate v0.1 summit band (4,000 m and up): the dome's visible top, mostly its skyline against the sky and the snow just below it
bands.upper: the plate v0.1 upper band (3,200-4,000 m): Gibraltar Rock, the upper Nisqually and Cowlitz glaciers, the top of Little Tahoma
bands.mid: the plate v0.1 mid band (2,400-3,200 m): the middle of the face, the Muir Snowfield ridge with Anvil Rock
bands.near: not labelled: the plate marks the near band not valid

states.visible: the band's terrain can be made out across about nine tenths of it or more
states.partial: a real part can be made out, but cloud covers about a tenth or more, or a veil clearly softens its edges
states.hidden: none of it, or only a small piece (about a tenth or less), can be made out; the camera itself is not in cloud
states.in_cloud: the camera itself is in cloud or fog (near trees and snow faded), and the band cannot be made out
states.unusable: the camera or the image, not the weather, stops the band being judged

protocol.merge_rule: where labellers a and b give a band the same state, that is its label (bands); where they differ the band's label is null: the frame is left out of that band's scoring and counted, and a sensitivity analysis scores it both ways
